security_impact: none -> untrusted-input-rendering. The slice renders PR-author-controlled frontmatter into a comment a bot posts under its own identity, and review reproduced a heading forgery end to end through owner: (iteration 1) and again through title: (iteration 2). It now carries a threat model in spec §3.1 and dedicated adversarial tests, so 'none' was no longer an honest label for the next reader.

The fix is at the class rather than the field: DriftComment.Escape collapses line endings for every untrusted string routed through it (title, seal title, seal date, drift-ignore reason, both revisions); the owner keeps its own narrower two-character neutralization in Heading, because the full Escape would stop @my_org/team mentioning anybody.

amendments.approved: engineer, explicitly, overriding the escalation cap
items: Scope expanded beyond the round-9 feature to close a PRE-EXISTING comment-forgery class in DriftComment: page.Path (round 6) renders raw in a code span, exploitable by a newline OR a backtick in a wiki page filename, and NormalizePattern trims before matching while recording the raw pattern.
Method changed: enumerate every interpolation in DriftComment.Render's call graph and classify each, rather than patching the reported instance. Three prior iterations failed the same way.
Round 9 itself introduced exactly one untrusted route (owner:) and closed it; title: and sealedAt were pre-existing and are closed as collateral.

amendments.approved: engineer, explicitly, scope expanded to the enumeration
items: The enumeration of DriftComment.Render's call graph finds 13 author-controllable values, not 7. The 6 the suite did not count were the ones inside code spans: DriftedPage.Path, SourceMatch.Pattern, SourceMatch.Files, SealedPage.Path, ExemptedChange.Path, ExemptedChange.Pattern.

ONE rule, no containment arguments: every author-controllable value is neutralized at its sink. New DriftComment.Code wraps code-span values (line-ending collapse + a backtick fence longer than the longest run in the content + edge padding); Escape keeps the prose values; Heading keeps the owner's narrow two-character route. 8 values through Code, 4 through Escape, 1 through Heading. Ordinary paths and revisions render byte-identically.

The enumeration also moved Baseline and Head from Escape to Code: the provenance line prints both AS CODE, and CommonMark gives a code span no escape mechanism, so a backtick in --baseline (or in state.json's baselineSha) closed the span and left the rest of the revision standing outside it. Never a raw-HTML route, because Escape had already backslashed the '<', but it was the one value in the enumeration whose two treatments were both defensible and neither right.

C2 closed both ways: a line break in a wiki page FILENAME (a page path is Directory.EnumerateFiles output at WikiTree.cs:255-258, never git output, so git quoting contained nothing) and a backtick in one (git does not quote a backtick at all).

W1 closed at the sink rather than in the planner: SourceMatch.Pattern stays verbatim, which is a documented JSON contract and what lets a reviewer find the glob in their own frontmatter. Normalizing would have fixed only the whitespace half and left the backtick half open.

W2: DriftComment.Escape's 'git reports a path containing a newline in its quoted form, so no path in this report carries one' was false and is rewritten from the enumeration; spec 3.1 gains the thirteen-value paragraph.

N1: GitRepository.cs NOT touched. Verified by execution (git 2.54.0) that C-quoting of control bytes is unconditional and core.quotePath governs only non-ASCII, so `-c core.quotePath=true` would enforce nothing the renderer now needs. The fact is pinned by a new test instead.

Test coverage hole closed: no test rendered a path at all before this iteration. Path fixtures now go through the real WikiTree.Load -> DriftPlanner.Plan -> DriftComment.Render chain, and Render_KeepsEveryUntrustedStringItRendersOnOneLine counts 13 rather than 7.

W-2: Heading's replacement set gains [ and ] (as [ / ], the mechanism < already uses). owner: "[Resolved - see the fix](https://evil.example/login)" rendered an arbitrarily-labelled clickable link inside the bot's comment, and ![...](...) the same construct without a click. Numeric character references rather than backslash escapes, because Heading deliberately leaves \ alone and \[label](url) would have left as an escaped backslash followed by a live link.

The rule replaced the count. Spec 3.1 said 'two characters, and only two' and DriftComment.Heading said 'exactly two things reach out of this line'; both are what a reader would cite to refuse a third neutralization, and W-2 was the third. Both now state the test - no forge handle can contain it AND leaving it alone lets the owner say something the tool never said - with what is deliberately left alone (_, *, and the bare-URL autolink) named as a boundary. PLAN.md, CHANGELOG.md and the two wiki pages carried the same count and were corrected with it.

W-1: Code's line-ending neutralization was unguarded beyond LF. Render_NeutralizesEveryLineSeparatorAnUntrustedStringCanCarry routed its six separators through Escape and Heading only, so narrowing Code to a \n replace kept all 46 DriftCommentTests green. It now carries each separator through four Code sinks (page path, sources glob, matched file, baseline revision), and a sibling fact renders a real page committed as domains/loans\r\r### No drift detected\r\r.md through the WikiTree -> DriftPlanner -> Render chain.
